title: Quantized inference perf: FP8/INT8 dynamic calibration + KV-eviction under mixed batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Establish a repeatable throughput/latency benchmark matrix for FP8 and INT8 quantized model variants that explicitly measures interactions between: (1) mixed-size batching (micro/standard/large), (2) long-context workflows with KV-cache reuse, and (3) dynamic vs static calibration pipelines. Goals: quantify end-to-end tail latency (p95/p99), average token throughput, and accuracy delta against FP32 baseline for representative LLMs (7B/13B). Deliverables: benchmark harness, calibration artifacts, consolidated dashboard, decision doc recommending default quant profiles per workload pattern.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Run on dedicated test fleet (nv-8xA100-sim nodes) with identical runtime knobs as staging.
- Test matrix covers: micro-batches (1,2), standard (8,16), large (32), and mixed arrival distributions that create microburst tails.
- Context lengths: 512, 2048, 8192. For long-context runs verify KV reuse hit-rate and measure eviction events.
- Compare FP32, FP8 (E4M3 & E5M2 flavors), INT8 per-channel symmetric, and INT8 per-tensor asymmetric where supported.
- Calibration: static offline calibration using representative corpora vs dynamic on-request calibration (warm-start with 100 samples + online adapt).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency per request, tokens/sec throughput, model quality: exact-match or semantic-similarity delta on validation prompts (~1,000 prompt set).

Test matrix (high level):
- Models: rwd-7b-base, rwd-13b-compact
- Batches: [1,2,8,16,32]; Mixed traffic pattern config file supplied in /bench/artifacts/mixed-load.json
- Contexts: [512,2048,8192]
- Quant variants: [fp32, fp8-e4m3, fp8-e5m2, int8-channel, int8-tensor]
- Calibration modes: [static-calib, dynamic-warmstart, dynamic-adapt]

Benchmark environment and scripts:
- Harness: bench/quant_longctx_runner.py (uses runtime bench API, continuous batching enabled, KV cache warm/cold toggles).
- Infra: test fleet labels runtime=test-quant-perf, driver image: redwood/runtime:1.28-quant-bench
- Artifacts: logs and CSVs written to s3://redwood-bench/quant/2026-03-*/; dashboards at https://hud.redwood.internal/d/quantization/longctx-batching

Hypotheses and risk areas:
1) FP8 (E4M3) will provide best throughput uplift for large batches but may show larger accuracy variance on long-context with adaptive KV casting.
2) INT8-channel will be stable for medium-length contexts but suffer worst p99 when KV-evictions are frequent due to extra dequant overhead and occasional kernel fallbacks.
3) Dynamic calibration reduces one-time cold-start loss but may introduce jitter in tail latency when calibration jobs contend with inference for memory bandwidth.

Initial instrumentation plan:
- Add tracing spans around: calibration job, quant-decode/encode kernel, KV-cache eviction, batch coalescing.
- Capture memory bandwidth util, PCIe saturations, and GPU kernel fallback events.

Acceptance thresholds for rollout recommendation:
- Throughput improvement >= 1.6x vs FP32 for any quant variant without exceeding +20% median accuracy delta on the validation set for production prompts.
- p99 tail latency for production-config batches must remain within SLA (<= 2x FP32 p99).

Notes on methodology differences from previous scans: we explicitly simulate mixed-size arrival distributions to exercise batching heuristics, and we track KV-cache eviction frequency as a first-class metric. This document avoids re-running standard quant calibration sweeps and instead focuses on interaction effects between quantization, batching, and long-context statefulness.
